COP1000.title: Introduction to Computer Programming
COP1000.prerequisites: None statewide, and no programming experience assumed. Some colleges recommend college-level math placement or MAT1033. Language and route vary by college - logic-first in pseudocode and flowcharts (Daytona State, Eastern Florida, Gulf Coast, Hillsborough, Northwest Florida), Python from day one (Pasco-Hernando), or a graphics/animation environment (FIU) - but SCNS equivalency is by number, not language. At FIU it may NOT be taken after COP 2210 or COP 2250: it is a precursor and does not advance the CS major. COP1000C (Broward, FSCJ, Valencia) is the same course with an integrated lab. Heading for a CS degree? Get the university department to confirm in writing which second programming course your college sequence satisfies - Florida numbers that course five different ways.

offering_notes.summary: Fifteen public carriers, all at 3 credits; no carrier of the unsuffixed number publishes contact hours. COP1000C is carried separately by Broward, FSCJ and Valencia at 3 credits.
offering_notes.derivation: Florida convention: 15 contact hours per credit for an unsuffixed lecture course, 3 x 15 = 45. FIU's Coursedog record leaves contact hours at 0 (unpublished). For comparison, Broward publishes 48 hours (32 lecture + 16 lab) for its COP1000C.

offerings.title: Principles of Computer Programming
offerings.note: Logic-first: algorithms, flowcharts, pseudocode, debugging, documentation and a high-level language. Offered fall, spring and summer.

offerings.title: Principles of Programming
offerings.note: Pseudocode and language-independent algorithms, with a current language as the demonstration platform; secure input validation. Lab fee.

offerings.title: Introduction to Computer Programming
offerings.note: Graphics and animation in a media programming environment for students with no prior experience. May not be taken after COP 2210 or COP 2250 - a precursor to FIU's majors sequence, not its first course.
